newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-HudCon, L.Lease bid for Docklands.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-HudCon, L.Lease bid for Docklands.

text.p: Hudson Conway Ltd said on Thursday that it and Lend Lease Corp Ltd would bid jointly for both Melbourne's proposed Docklands Stadium and the overall A$2 billion Melbourne Docklands redevelopment.
The special purpose joint venture, to be known as the Lend Lease-Hudson Conway Consortium, would have combined total assets of A$4.5 billion, Hudson Conway said.

"The combined financial and operating strengths of the two groups will substantially enhance the prospects for a successful tender for the Melbourne docklands project," Hudson Conway chief executive Lloyd Williams said in a statement.

The 52,000-seat stadium, estimated to cost between A$200 million and A$300 million, is planned to be the centrepiece of the revitalisation of the docklands area on the western edge of Melbourne's central business district.
Hudson Conway and Lend Lease were both on a shortlist of five companies announced at the end of last month by Victoria's Docklands Authority.

Hudson Conway said the redevelopment of the docklands site would include industrial, residential, commercial and retail elements, as well as a significant amount of public parkland and a promenade area.
The stadium is the first of five planned Docklands development precincts on the 220-hectare site.
The Docklands Authority, which is overseeing the entire development project, said on Thursday that another four bidders had been amalgamated into a rival consortium.
These were Thiess Contractors, International Business Park, Yarra Waters and Terminus Consortium, authority chairman Eric Mayer said in a separate statement.
Bid proposals for the five Docklands precincts are due to be submitted by April 11, the authority said.
Lend Lease Property Group chief executive Steve McMillan said the Victorian government had yet to decide whether to award all five to one group or to select different developers.
"There's a long, long way to go on this and the timetable isn't clearly established," he told Reuters.
"We just think it's a very good combination of outfits."
"These are very large projects and we don't want to do them all on our own," he said.
